notes: The todo list for making the APK the web (#882): one row per surface in perf/surfaces.json, in the order the work is meant to happen, and the state of each. `native` is only when the row in docs/mobile/screens.json says `enabled: true` and its evidence passes check:visual (ADR-0118); `todo` is a surface the app still opens in the document and means to port; `document` is one where the page is the deliverable, and `why` says what makes a native copy wrong (ADR-0178); `blocked` is one that cannot be worked yet, and `blockedBy` says why. `release` is the half a surface list cannot hold - the cutover, the diagnostics screen, the device measurements - each `done` with its evidence or `open` with what closes it. check:plan fails when a surface has no row, a row names a surface that does not exist, the two files disagree about what is on, a document row gives no reason, a release item is done without evidence, or a ported component in docs/mobile/parity.json belongs to a surface this plan does not know. docs/mobile/parity-plan.md and the tracking issue are generated from this file - do not hand-edit either.

phases.title: Prove the gate
phases.why: The three surfaces that already have a Kotlin screen. Recording both sides here exercises the harness on screens that exist, before a single line of new drawing.

phases.title: Public content
phases.why: Read with no session, so the page can be recorded without the fixture account and a failure is about the screen rather than about data.

phases.title: Sign-in
phases.why: The site is what signs in until the cutover, and the native flow is what makes the cutover possible: a Custom Tab cannot set the app's session.

phases.title: The app's core
phases.why: The account area, notifications and chats: the screens a member opens daily.

phases.title: Products
phases.why: The local-store products, where the app has a real reason to be native: offline writes and a device store behind the same screen.

phases.title: Requests and bookings
phases.why: Forms that end in a server write, so a port has to bring the same validation and the same confirmation as the page.

phases.title: Operator surfaces
phases.why: Listed so nothing is missing, and blocked as one decision: the admin area needs its own security review before any of it is drawn natively (#660).

phases.title: The door
phases.why: The homepage hosts the nine apps as tabs under the strip (ADR-0146), so it comes after every app it can host: a tab whose app is still the document is a tab that leaves the door.

surfaces.why: Five static pages (`/pricing`, `/privacy`, `/security`, `/terms`, `/app-info`): words the site owns and changes without an APK. The document is the page, so a policy edit costs a deploy and no release.

surfaces.blockedBy: hidden from the UI; the page stays reachable by direct URL but is not a port target

surfaces.why: A guide: prose and one paste-ready snippet, owned by the site. A native copy would be wrong the first time the server's MCP surface moves, for an interaction a port does not improve.
A one-time setup page whose whole value is the snippet it shows. The page changes with the server, and a port would pin a snippet the server no longer accepts.

A decision, not a queue item: the sheet is the apps surface, and `/mcp/apps` stays the address a callback, a bookmark and a deep link need (ADR-0159, #1385). The sheet is native; the page is what a link resolves to.

surfaces.blockedBy: the cutover: once the WebView leaves, a Custom Tab cannot set the app's session, so sign-in has to be native - password and OTP on screen, Google through a Custom Tab and the `royar://auth` return, and the Keystore session written back into the document cookie while one is still in front (ADR-0178)

surfaces.why: The member's own post management, opened rarely: the post card is already native in the feed, and the page's writes are server actions. Revisit when posting from the phone becomes a first-class flow - a creator surface, draft management, or usage that shows people opening it.

surfaces.blockedBy: no door on the web: the page is the request, booking and training forms, which left the UI in ADR-0148; leads and consultation are blocked for the same reason

no door on the web (ADR-0148), so there is no page to compare a screen against. The port that was never reached - screen, store and tests - was deleted in the change that added the `document` state (ADR-0178), so nothing is owed here.

no door on the web: `consultation/book` left the picker with the other lead forms (ADR-0148) and the site links it nowhere. Its port was deleted with the lead forms' (ADR-0178), so nothing is owed here.
the nine tabs need nine native screens: `athkar` and `notes` are the two that do not have one

release.title: The app reports its own failures
Remove the Capacitor bridge: MainActivity, ShellPlugins, capacitor.config.ts, WebSurface and DocumentCookies
release.why: Phase 5 (ADR-0089). Until the bridge leaves, the APK ships a WebView and every `document` route is the live site inside it.

release.title: Give every `document` surface a renderer after the WebView goes
release.why: A Custom Tab is the system browser rather than an in-APK WebView, so it keeps the `document` rows as the page through the cutover (ADR-0178).

release.title: A diagnostics screen replacing /device
release.why: Phase 2 exit (ADR-0084): an APK has no console and no page to inspect.

release.title: A remote-config switch that opens one surface in a Custom Tab
release.why: Phase 4 exit (native-app.md): without it a broken native screen is an emergency release.

release.title: A sign-in claims the guest Local Store's rows
release.why: Owed since #768 (ADR-0107): the guest store exists and is empty until a guest can write, and a guest's rows would be stranded at sign-in.

release.title: HabitFlow's add form and delete affordance
release.why: Owed since #650: the store, transport and fixtures cover create, update, toggle and delete; the screen exposes the toggle.

release.title: The FCM wake on a real device, backgrounded and killed, and the 15-minute floor
release.why: Three rows of the real-device matrix are unverified; google-services.json is present, so the build they need exists (docs/mobile/android-shell.md).

release.title: Measure 500 rows at 60 fps on the RMX3195
release.why: The one native budget with no witness (docs/mobile/native-app.md).
